**Working manuscript, not a completed experimental report.** The evidence
cutoff is 12 September 2026. Nine of ten selected reference executions were
accepted. The nine-scenario warehouse-only retry passed independent solution
and service checks but did not complete all three lexicographic passes; final
HPC acceptance remains pending. Author order, affiliations, ORCIDs and email
addresses were supplied by the research lead. Contributions and final manuscript
approval remain to be documented.

# Introduction

Grain-storage investment is simultaneously a location problem and a network
planning problem. A storage facility connects seasonal arrivals to consumption
and export outlets, while its static capacity and handling throughput constrain
different activities. A building with sufficient stock capacity may still be
unable to receive a harvest peak. Conversely, more reception throughput cannot
create an outlet for supply when the selected network is disconnected.

The literature provides complementary perspectives on these decisions.
@foulds2005 develops dynamic network-flow models for grain-silo location.
@dubke2011 studies specialized terminals in Brazilian soybean exports, and
@steiner2017 examines a multi-objective approach to silo location in Paraná.
The review by @rosa2025 motivates integrating storage-location decisions with
uncertainty and heterogeneous warehouse and grain characteristics. These works
support an integrated research question: how can an investment model remain
useful to public planning while making its data transformations, feasibility
relaxations and computational limits explicit?

Model Agrologistic addresses that question as a technological research
demonstrator, not a deployed procurement system. The intended contribution is
an auditable chain from input data to a qualified planning result. Three
objectives guide the study: reconstruct a documented thesis-method baseline;
separate and explain policy extensions; and validate selected deterministic and
stochastic computations in an HPC environment. The study does not seek to prove
that a single modeled investment plan is unique or immediately implementable.

# Related work and research positioning

Storage-network design and agricultural decision support operate at different
decision horizons. @mardaneh2021 presents a decision-support system for grain
harvesting, storage and distribution. In soybean tactical planning,
@reis2023 uses a two-stage stochastic linear program whose first-stage decisions
concern purchasing and contracted transport. Our strategic first stage instead
concerns warehouse investment. Their reported monetary gains therefore cannot
serve as a numerical benchmark for the present model.

The intermodal hub-disruption setting of @maiyar2019 is also distinct from the
road-distance representation used here. It motivates treating network
availability as a modeling assumption rather than interpreting every missing
arc as a geographic impossibility. We do not claim to implement their
disruption model, a multimodal network, a genetic algorithm or a new solution
algorithm. The literature selection is a focused narrative review of relevant
items supplied by the maintainer and verified in local Zotero metadata; it is
not a new systematic literature review.

# Mathematical framework

## Decisions, stages and physical units

Let $W$ denote warehouses, $O$ supply origins, $C$ customers, $P$ products,
$T$ periods and $S$ scenarios with probabilities $\pi_s$. Customers have
separate domestic and export roles. First-stage decisions $x$ include candidate
opening, expansion and bulk-handling conversion. The same $x$ applies to all
scenarios. Recourse contains nonnegative transported quantities, inventory and
explicit feasibility slacks. A deterministic case is the single-scenario
specialization. The following equations summarize the contract, rather than
replace the indexed formulation and independent validator in the repository.

For an eligible warehouse, nominal static capacity is $K_w(x)$ in tonnes.
Reception and shipping rates are $R_w(x)$ and $H_w(x)$ in tonnes/day.
Operating days $d_t$ convert those rates to period throughput. With inventory
$I_{wpts}$, total inbound and outbound flows $F^{in}_{wts}$ and $F^{out}_{wts}$,
and separate static and reception slacks $e^K_{wts}$ and $e^R_{wts}$:

$$
\sum_p I_{wpts}\le K_w(x)+e^K_{wts},\qquad
F^{in}_{wts}\le d_tR_w(x)+e^R_{wts},\qquad
F^{out}_{wts}\le d_tH_w(x).
$$ {#eq-capacity}

Both slacks in @eq-capacity have a tonne-based constraint unit, but describe
different mechanisms. Reception slack is **period overflow**, not a daily
rate: multiplying it by 30 would convert it twice. Its daily equivalent for
reporting is $e^R_{wts}/d_t$. Static exceedance summed over periods is an
accumulated stock-violation measure, not the capacity of a building to construct.
Bulkification improves handling through declared daily factors; it does not
automatically create static capacity. Expansion and bulkification are mutually
exclusive at each eligible warehouse in the current contract.

Candidate nominal capacity is linked to opening. Additional activation
constraints set both emergency slacks to zero at a closed candidate; otherwise
the relaxation could create an unactivated warehouse. Shipping, route eligibility
and activation remain hard restrictions. Thus, the model has a **conditional
feasibility relaxation**, not unconditional complete recourse for arbitrary data.

## Conservation and service

Every origin's supplied quantity must enter an eligible outbound flow; the
model has no unallocated-supply or disposal decision. Product-specific warehouse
balances carry initial inventory through successive periods. Domestic service
uses an equality with unmet demand $u_{cpts}$:

$$
F^{dom}_{cpts}+u_{cpts}=D_{cpts},\qquad u_{cpts}\ge0.
$$ {#eq-service}

Export flow is subject to its declared upper bound, including explicitly
unbounded export roles. Terminal inventory is free, subject to the period
balance and capacity system. For each scenario, the global check is

$$
\text{supply}+\text{initial inventory}
=\text{domestic flow}+\text{export flow}+\text{terminal inventory}.
$$ {#eq-balance}

This check is necessary but insufficient: local product-period residuals could
cancel in an aggregate. The independent validator therefore reconstructs local
balances, capacity restrictions, activation, investment eligibility and costs.
Domestic fulfillment is interpreted per scenario as well as in aggregate.

## Penalties and the policy hierarchy

For a common scalar objective, the two-stage recourse problem has the form

$$
Z_{RP}=\min_x\left\{C^{inv}(x)+
\sum_{s\in S}\pi_s\min_{y_s}\left[C^{op}(x,y_s)+P_s(y_s)\right]\right\},
$$ {#eq-rp}

where $P_s$ contains explicitly reported shortage and capacity penalties.
Dynamic Big-M coefficients are algorithmic feasibility penalties, not observed
social costs. They are frozen with the selected network before any stochastic
projection. They must not be used to claim a financial return on infrastructure
without an independently defensible monetary calibration.

Separate slacks are an intentional departure from the historical shared-slack
construction. For fixed simultaneous exceedances $a,b$ and common rate $P$,
shared penalization gives $P\max(a,b)$, while separation gives $P(a+b)$.
Consequently, reproducing selected thesis parameters does not establish
numerical equivalence of the resulting objective or investment decisions.

The policy extension instead applies a service-first hierarchy:

$$
\operatorname{lexmin}\left(
\mathbb E\!\left[\sum u\right],
\mathbb E\!\left[\sum(e^K+e^R)\right],
C^{inv}+\mathbb E[C^{op}]
\right).
$$ {#eq-hierarchy}

The second component is an equal-weight **violation score**, not an installed
capacity recommendation. The hierarchy prevents an economic saving from
silently substituting for the chosen domestic-service priority. Nevertheless,
mixed-integer and objective-degradation tolerances matter: pass-end objectives,
final objectives, bounds and completion statuses are all reported. We do not
equate a solver's tolerance-qualified `optimal` status with an exact mathematical
optimum. Emergency use is admissible evidence of a gap within the modeled
network and investment options; it is not by itself a failed experiment.

# Data lineage and network construction

The study separates the historical benchmark source pool, a normalized bounded
instance, and an expanded canonical workbook. Duplicate-key normalization
preserves material totals; candidate translation distinguishes registry
placeholders from genuine investment costs. The policy reference contains 215
warehouses, comprising 146 existing facilities and 69 candidates. A nested
500-warehouse input was also materialized, but that fact is **not evidence of
a successfully optimized 500-warehouse instance**.

OSRM v6.0.0, the driving profile, MLD preprocessing and the dated
`brazil-260901` extract define the road-distance authority. Distances are
materialized before optimization; the solver never queries a live routing
service. The Table service returns distance along the profile-selected fastest
route, which is not necessarily the shortest-distance road path. Ordered
coordinate pairs, dataset/profile identity and query policy identify cached
entries. Routing failures do not silently become straight-line distances.
Only declared no-route or excessive-snap cases admit audited Haversine fallback.
The two materialized policy populations were reported to require no fallback.

The historical grouped rule retains the nearest ceiling 20 percent of eligible
edges per sending-node/product group. It is a sparsification rule, not a proof
of Pareto optimality. The policy profile adds explicit connectivity repairs
from eligible routes when required; added edges are reported separately. Direct
origin-to-customer arcs form a controlled on/off factor. Interwarehouse freight
uses a separate interhub factor, $\alpha$. Physical routing coverage and
post-filter customer reachability are different diagnostics.

The present OSM snapshot and the unreconstructed forecasting path differ from
the thesis inputs. Accordingly, the correct claim is a bounded **thesis-method
comparison with separate slacks**, followed by a policy extension. Exact
replication of published thesis cost tables is not an acceptance criterion.

# Experimental and validation protocol

The selected reference design is deliberately smaller than the available
factorial configuration space. @tbl-design describes the comparison
without exposing internal gate numbers as scientific treatment labels.

| Profile | Scenarios | Direct arcs | Interpretation |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Bounded thesis-method | 1 and 3 | Off / on | $\alpha=0.8$, grouped 20 percent, separate slacks |
| Policy, 215 warehouses | 1, 3 and 9 | Off / on | Service-first, 20 percent plus connectivity repair |

: Selected reference design: four thesis-method and six policy executions. {#tbl-design}

The coupled three-scenario thesis profile uses probabilities 0.33, 0.34 and
0.33 with low, central and high supply/demand factors. Policy scenarios are
defined in separate versioned manifests; their design is not an empirical
probability forecast. Three versus nine scenarios therefore compares specified
experimental distributions, not a statistical convergence guarantee.

Gurobi is the reference backend. SCIP is a reserved extension, not an implemented
alternative in this study. Selected nine-scenario retries permit 14,400 seconds
of optimization. The objective is to establish a bounded functional
demonstration, not a definitive complexity threshold. Larger warehouse
populations, a complete 15/20/25-percent sensitivity campaign and solver
comparisons are outside the current critical path.

Validation has four levels: mathematical/data contracts; software and licensed
analytical tests; independent solution validation; and the selected HPC
demonstration. Acceptance requires matching implementation, runtime, data and
configuration identities. Old evidence remains attached to its original
identity even when later source changes are only documentation changes.

Data reading, backend construction and `model.optimize()` have separate clocks.
Post-optimality computations for stochastic-value analysis require additional
solves and must be reported separately from primary optimization. Slurm elapsed
time includes orchestration and must not substitute for the optimizer clock.
An end-to-end reporting table must distinguish these intervals and disclose
cache reuse rather than adding overlapping measurements.

## Value of information and stochasticity

For comparable minimization problems on the same frozen scalar objective,

$$
EVPI=Z_{RP}-Z_{WS},\qquad VSS=Z_{EEV}-Z_{RP}.
$$ {#eq-values}

WS optimizes first-stage decisions independently by scenario; EEV evaluates the
expected-value investment plan in the stochastic environment. Both metrics
require additional optimization and component-level cost accounting. A large
penalty-driven VSS is not a monetized economic benefit. Investment, operating
and penalty differences must be presented separately.

If $L$ and $U$ denote valid objective bounds and incumbent values, an EVPI
interval is $[L_{RP}-U_{WS},\ U_{RP}-L_{WS}]$; similarly a VSS interval is
$[L_{EEV}-U_{RP},\ U_{EEV}-L_{RP}]$. An interval crossing zero is numerically
indeterminate, not evidence of negative theoretical stochastic value. Classical
monetary EVPI/VSS is not automatically assigned to the service-first vector
objective in @eq-hierarchy.

# Evidence status and planned results presentation

At the stated cutoff, the maintainer-supplied validation report accepts levels
1-3 and nine selected references. Overall acceptance is rejected because the
nine-scenario warehouse-only retry lacks three completed lexicographic passes;
level 4 remains pending. Its independently validated incumbent does not establish
completion of the objective hierarchy. The nine-scenario direct-arc retry is accepted.
Therefore, final objective, investment, service, capacity-gap and stochastic-value
tables are deliberately withheld. Older exploratory CSVs use different
contracts and cannot fill these cells. This is a pending evidence boundary,
not a missing value to replace by zero or a synthetic example.

The completed report will use separate deterministic and stochastic summary
tables: investment and operating costs, penalties, warehouse decisions,
domestic service, dynamic capacity, turnover, objective bounds and timings.
Transport work will be expressed in tonne-kilometres and broken down by OD,
DC, DD and OC arcs. Inventory heatmaps will compare matched warehouse-period
cells; scenario spreads will be labeled as scenario ranges rather than
confidence intervals. Warehouse-level profiles will distinguish opening,
expansion, bulkification, stock exceedance and reception overflow. Cost
composition plots will disclose whether their denominator includes penalties.

These outputs are the intended counterparts to the thesis's cost, transport,
warehouse-profile and stock-comparison presentations, not copied figures.
Formal thesis bibliographic metadata and the final figure/table correspondence
remain editorial prerequisites. Dynamic-capacity and turnover captions must
state the implemented denominator and time basis before numerical comparison.

# Discussion and limitations

The development already establishes why model and data contracts matter.
Changing the distance authority can change the retained network. Changing
shared to separate slacks can change penalties even for fixed physical
violations. Replacing scalar penalization with a hierarchy changes the decision
criterion, not merely the solver configuration. These are substantive modeling
choices and should not be disguised as implementation details.

For public administration, emergency quantities identify where the modeled
system struggles under the available investment options. They are conditional
diagnostics, influenced by candidate limits, selected routes, operating days,
penalties or hierarchy weights and scenario design. Translating them into
capital projects requires engineering, budget and regional feasibility work.
The model does not establish causal welfare gains, resolve unmodeled rail or
waterway connectivity, or justify arbitrary fixed investment charges.

The bounded experimental design also limits generalization. A successful
solver run does not establish data realism, a unique investment plan or
performance on every larger network. Likewise, the previously accepted v0.1
demonstrator package documents a development milestone; it is not an external
TRL accreditation and does not certify this changed v0.2 formulation.

# Conclusions

This work organizes strategic grain-storage optimization around explicit
mathematical contracts and traceable computational evidence. Its key design
choice is to distinguish service fulfillment, capacity inadequacy and economic
cost rather than treating a large penalized objective as a single substantive
result. The current manuscript establishes the framework and publication
contract. Quantitative findings and planning implications will be finalized
only after the remaining selected HPC evidence is independently accepted.

# Reproducibility and availability

The source repository is
[Model Agrologistic](https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic).
At this draft's cutoff the repository is public and GitHub Pages is enabled;
the maintainer reports GitHub Actions as the publishing source. Configuration
alone does not establish deployment of this working manuscript.
The manuscript uses the pinned
[quarto-sbc template](https://github.com/cvictorr2508/quarto-sbc/tree/88eaa11eeee9f86cd8594466e4644b321c8d7b75).
Its HTML and SBC PDF builds execute no solver, do not contact Zotero and require
no NPAD credentials. Bibliography metadata is committed; local library notes,
attachments, licenses and raw HPC working directories are not publication inputs.

The repository includes the mathematical contract, reference manifests,
independent-validation implementation and publication instructions. Final
publication requires a reviewed frozen evidence package and final manuscript
approval. Public data availability and third-party licensing must be checked
before publishing additional artifacts. Rendering successfully certifies document construction,
not scientific acceptance.
